discovery observed\n description-experiment Propose, start, or read a two-arm tool-description\n
rewrite experiment\n cancel [options] Cancel an in-flight eval run (no-op if already\n
cancelled; errors if it already finished)\n rerun [options] <run-id> Rerun a finished eval run's failed cases as
a new\n run. The platform picks the cases: any with a trial\n that did not
complete and pass (cancelled and\n skipped trials do not count)\n judge-backtest [options] Preview
draft grading instructions on recorded\n evidence (uses credits)\n backtest [options] Previe
w assertion changes on stored evidence\n without changing results\n judge [options] Grade
a finished eval run with LLM as Judge (SPENDS\n your model budget)\n github Run a
n eval suite on a GitHub repository's pull\n requests (GitHub checks)\n checks De
precated alias for `cloud eval github` — a\n repository's GitHub checks, not a case's grading\n
checks\n iterations [options] List per-iteration results for an eval run\n
(pass/fail, tool calls, tokens, latency)\n gate [options] Apply a pass/fail policy to a finished eval run and\n
set an exit code (0 pass or waived, 1 eval failure,\n 2 usage, 3 incomplete)\
n compare [options] Compare a finished eval run against a baseline and\n set an exit code (0
pass, 1 regression, 2 usage, 3\n incomplete)\n validate [options] Validate a local eval suit
e file offline — no auth,\n no network unless --project is passed (0 valid, 1\n
contract-invalid or unresolved reference, 2\n unreadable/oversize/malformed)\n export [options]
Write a hosted eval suite to a local suite file,\n refusing anything it cannot represent lo
sslessly\n pull [options] LEGACY: materialize a hosted eval suite into a\n corpus lock fo
r @mcpjam/vitest — new work should\n use `eval export` (0 clean, 1 drift under --frozen,\n
2 usage, 3 incomplete)\n trace [options] Fetch the full trace for one eval iteration (large:\n
full message history + spans)\n steps [options] Per-authored-step results for one eval iteration
:\n status (ok/fail/skipped/pending), reason, and\n evidence (screenshot/v
ideo URLs). The fastest way\n to see WHICH step failed and why.\n screenshot [options] Show the
widget screenshot(s) an eval iteration\n rendered — inline when the terminal supports it,\n
otherwise the image URL\n video [options] Get the replay recording an eval iteration made —\n
prints the URL, or downloads it with --out. A local\n widget run records a .web
m; an unattended run on a\n hosted browser records an .mp4\n get [options] Show an eval
suite's full settings\n update [options] Edit an eval suite's settings (only the flags you\n
pass change)\n delete [options] Permanently delete an eval suite (and its cases and\n run
s)\n schedule [options] Enable or disable scheduled runs for a suite\n environments Attach or detach the p
roject environments an eval\n suite runs against\n cases List, author, and edit

an eval suite's test cases

Index\n> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.mcpjam.com/llms.txt\n> Use this file to discover all available p

ages before exploring further.

# Local Evals

> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine with mcpjam test with local res

ults and an MCPJam identity

> [!NOTE]
>
> The upcoming SDK 10, CLI 6, and Vitest 0.3 releases require an MCPJam login or `sk_
` API key for every eval, including BYOK runs with uploads disabled. These versions must ship after the backend run-start endpoint
is deployed. Earlier versions keep their existing behavior.\n\n`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connect
s your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses,
and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your own provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-ho
sted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.\n\nResults are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to your
terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the run start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single an
onymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.md) event, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off; the run

adds no telemetry of its own.

## Eval identity and local data

Run `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` to
an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK also accepts `apiKey` or `mcpjamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take precedenc
e over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, which takes precedence over the saved CLI login. An invalid explicit credential never falls back to anoth
er account. CI never starts an interactive login. Ask an organization admin for a key if you cannot create one.\n\nEvery logical r
un needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transient failures within ten seconds, then stops before execution. A prior succ
essful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI resolves the project using its existing `--project`, environment, and linked
-project settings; a key can only access its own organization.\n\nWith results uploads disabled, the start-run request sends only
the credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API headers you configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam`, proj
ect selection, a new run-start ID, client version and surface (SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider names, and
whether a client profile is used (`unknown` for custom executors). The server resolves the organization and account. The start-run
request sends no prompts, outputs, tool calls, or server URLs. MCPJam-hosted inference still sends prompts through MCPJam to the
model, as before. Retries reuse the same ID. Planned iterations are intent, not completed usage or a charge. This release adds no
debit, quota draw, or balance refusal.\n\n`DO_NOT_TRACK`, `MCPJAM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, and CLI telemetry settings disable analytic
